folios.title: Pick a side
folios.updated_copy: Kevin Zeek stopped at the break in the vegetation. Rain had erased the easy-looking path, leaving roots slick and mud deep enough to steal a stride. Last week he had watched water undo his own defenses. He was not about to let Phillip see him hesitate. 'Race you to the dry stone.' Phillip Pitts turned all three heads toward the opening. 'You sure you want the short way?' Kevin grinned. 'I usually do.' He took the direct approach; Phillip followed the longer, firmer edge of the same visitor-side clearing.

folios.production_locked_dialogue: Race you to the dry stone.
folios.production_performance: Kevin’s speed loses to Phillip’s local knowledge; rivalry ends with dry wit.
folios.production_explicit_hold: No bounty costume or bag. Visitor-side clearing only; informal challenge proposed, no World promotion. One body, three heads.

folios.title: The dry stone
folios.updated_copy: Kevin had the first few strides. Then the mud caught his foot and he had to steady himself against a root. Across the clearing Phillip kept moving, one head watching the ground, another tracking Kevin, the third fixed on the sheltered stone. When Kevin reached it, Phillip was already waiting. Kevin looked down at his muddy legs. 'You should see me on dry ground.' Phillip glanced at the stone beneath them. 'All three of us would love to.' Kevin laughed despite himself. The Snake had won on his own ground, 125.74 to 94.80.
